name: Pauli phase gadget removal
summary: A spider connected only to an X-spider with phase aπ and, by Hadamard edges, to some neighbours can be removed by adding aπ to all of its neighbours.
description:
Let $u$ be a phase-free Z-spider whose only plain leg ends in an X-spider with phase $a\pi$ ($a\in\{0,1\}$), and which is connected to its neighbours by Hadamard edges. Then $u$ can be deleted, together with its edges, at the cost of adding $a\pi$ to every neighbour. In graph-like form, $u$ is a phase gadget with a Pauli phase: a phase gadget with phase $\pi$ is the tensor product of Pauli Z's on its targets, and a phase gadget with phase 0 is the identity.

In MBQC language, this says that a qubit measured in the Z basis (a YZ- or XZ-plane measurement with a Pauli angle) can be removed from a graph state, with Pauli Z corrections on its neighbours. Read from right to left, with $a=0$, it inserts a new vertex with arbitrary neighbours ('Z-insertion'), which is used in proofs of flow-preserving completeness. If $u$ has a phase $\beta$ (e.g. $\frac\pi2$, the XZ-plane case), the same holds with an additional scalar $e^{ia\beta}$.
parameter_notes: n is the number of neighbours of u (shown for n = 3). The neighbours may have any phases and any number of further legs and edges; aπ is added to their phases.

source.location: Section 4.3 (Removing Clifford vertices), lemma on YZ/XZ-plane Pauli measurements
